questions.question: What should we prioritize for the Nov 11 outage?
must: Lead with the reel drum DS bearing: Bonvoy has flagged it since Jul 21, the Keel route confirmed an outer race defect on Aug 12 (0.17 in/s), it missed the Aug 19 outage because the bearing (22238 CCK/W33) wasn't in stores, and it read 0.39 in/s on the Oct 14 route (Danger is 0.40); the WO is in the Nov 11 scope waiting on parts, ETA Nov 5. Then both refiner plate changes (REF 1 due, REF 2 early because its plates are wearing fast) with only one Ridgeway set on hand, the 3rd section DS rotary joint replacement Brightwater recommends after three seal failures, and the two jobs with parts not reserved (couch roll seal strips, 2nd section PV fan belts).

questions.question: Why did we change the 2nd press top felt early in May?
must: It filled in about three weeks: Uhle box vacuum climbed from late April (Bonvoy flagged it from May 10), press solids fell and the 4th section steam hit its limit on 34 Super, holding speed back. The Spraywell audit on May 13 found 22% of the 2nd press top HP shower nozzles plugged and the supply strainer packed. The felt came out on May 19 after 34 days (target 42) in a 7.5 h shut; Marlow's analysis found 71% fill. RCFA-SM-26-016 is still open: the action to add Uhle vacuum rate of rise to Bonvoy is overdue.

questions.question: Chart REF 1 against REF 2 specific energy since the Sep 30 outage. At this rate, where will REF 2 be on Nov 11?
must: REF 1 holds steady at about 61–63 kWh/t. REF 2 ran with it until about Oct 8, then climbed about 1.4% a day to about 81 kWh/t on Oct 31 (daily average). Carried on, that is roughly 92–95 kWh/t by Nov 11: an extrapolation, not a forecast. Both plate sets are due on Nov 11 and there is one Ridgeway set on hand, so the second set needs ordering now (that action is overdue). Chart: two lines from Oct 1, the projection dashed, the outage marked.

questions.question: Chart the Nov 11 outage scope by parts status and list what isn't ready.
must: 22 work orders: 17 with parts reserved, 4 not reserved and 1 on order. Not ready: change REF 1 and REF 2 refiner plates (one set on hand for two changes), rebuild the couch roll seal strips, replace the 2nd section PV fan belts and sheaves (all four at status 30, parts not reserved), and the reel drum DS bearing change (status 45, bearing on order, ETA Nov 5). Chart: WO count by parts status.

questions.question: Write tomorrow's BUS line for REF 2 and say who should own it.
must: Area: Refiners · Position: REF 2 · Issue: specific energy climbing about 1.4%/day on the Sep 30 plates, about 81 kWh/t against 62 on REF 1; Ridgeway suspects sand carry-over · Action: order the second 34" LC plate set today so both refiners can be changed on Nov 11 (one set on hand) · Owner: Quentin Adeyemi, who has the overdue plate order action (due Oct 28); Tobias Renner owns the current BUS item. WOs: the two Nov 11 plate changes, parts not reserved.

questions.question: Which repeat failures don't have an RCFA?
must: The 3rd section DS rotary joint: three steam leaks (Jan 6, Jun 23, Oct 2), about 8 h down in all, each under the 3 h RCFA threshold and more than 60 days apart, so none triggered an RCFA. Bonvoy saw the 3rd section syphon differential drop for days before each one. Brightwater's Oct 14 survey says the joint is misaligned on its bracket and seal kits alone will keep failing: replace and re-align it at the next outage. (The headbox slime stops and the forming fabric stops repeat too, but each has RCFAs.)

questions.question: Is the reel drum bearing temperature following the vibration? Plot both since mid-July.
must: Yes. Both were flat until late July and have climbed together since: vibration from about 0.06 to about 0.43 in/s on Oct 31 (past Danger at 0.40) and DS bearing temperature from about 134 to about 168 °F. Neither has levelled off, which fits the outer race defect the Keel route found on Aug 12 getting worse. The change is in the Nov 11 scope with the bearing on order. Chart: vibration on the left axis, temperature on the right, the 0.40 Danger line marked.

questions.question: If the reel drum bearing keeps rising, will it hit Danger before Nov 11?
must: It already has. Daily average vibration crossed the 0.40 in/s Danger level around Oct 22 and was about 0.43 on Oct 31, still rising. The change (outer race defect found on the Aug 12 Keel route) is in the Nov 11 scope, waiting on the 22238 CCK/W33 bearing (ETA Nov 5; the expedite action is overdue). Until then: closer checks on the bearing and a plan for an unplanned change if it gets worse.

questions.question: Do we break more on 24# than on 34 Super? Chart it.
must: Yes, but by less than the raw counts suggest. 24# has 402 of the 578 breaks (70%), but it also ran 64% of the hours (about 5,600 h). Per 100 h run: 24# 7.2, 28# 6.7 (only 238 h, so a small sample), 31# 6.1 and 34 Super 5.2. So 24# breaks about 40% more often per hour than 34 Super. Chart: breaks per 100 h by grade.

questions.question: Is one crew breaking more than the others? Show it on a chart.
must: B has the most breaks (164) and A the fewest (122), with C 147 and D 145. On DuPont 12 the four crews work the same hours, so the counts compare directly. B against A alone is a real-looking gap (about 2.5 standard deviations), but across all four crews the spread is close to what chance gives (chi-square p about 0.1). Worth watching, not proof of a crew problem; grade mix on each crew's shifts is the next thing to check. Chart: breaks by crew.

questions.question: When was the calender bottom roll last ground?
must: Sim Mill's PM1 has no calender: the sheet goes from the 4th dryer section straight to the reel. There's no calender roll in My Machine, the work orders or the vendor reports. The rolls with grind history are the press rolls, the couch roll and the reel and winder drums, if one of those was meant.

questions.question: What actions are overdue?
must: Eleven, oldest first. Nine are RCFA actions: MCC room cooling (RCFA-SM-26-007, due Apr 20), the wad detector camera (RCFA-SM-26-006, due Apr 30), Uhle vacuum rate-of-rise shift checks for the 1st press bottom felt (RCFA-SM-26-015) and on Bonvoy (RCFA-SM-26-016, the 2nd press top felt), hood exhaust fan belts on the monthly PM (RCFA-SM-26-017), the felt design review (RCFA-SM-26-014), the grease reviews for the pulper rotor and the dryer drive lineup (RCFA-SM-26-013, -026) and the shower strainer on the outage clean list (RCFA-SM-26-024). Two are for the Nov 11 outage: expediting the reel drum bearing (due Oct 15) and ordering the second set of refiner plates (due Oct 28).
